name: AMD Infinity Fabric link (4th generation, CDNA 4 / MI350 class)
version: CDNA 4 / AMD Instinct MI350 Series (MI350X, MI355X)
bandwidth_basis: PER LINK, PER DIRECTION - DIRECTION NOW STATED BY AMD ITSELF, which removes the ambiguity that forced amd-infinity-fabric-link to be contested for three audit passes. The CDNA 4 white paper (net2-amd-cdna4-whitepaper) says verbatim: 'The AMD CDNA 4 architecture comprises 8 AMD Infinity Fabric links that are 16-bits wide and fully bi-directional' and 'The Infinity Fabric links in the AMD CDNA 4 architecture run up to 20% faster generationally at 38.4Gbps for a total link bandwidth of 76.8GB/s IN EACH DIRECTION'. Endnote MI350-007 gives the matching aggregate: 'up to 153.6 GB/s peak total aggregate theoretical transport data GPU peer-to-peer (P2P) bandwidth per AMD Infinity Fabric link', and 'up to eight AMD Infinity Fabric links providing up to 1,075.2 GB/s peak aggregate peer-to-peer (P2P) and 1,203.2 total peak aggregate theoretical GPU transport rate bandwidth performance per GPU OAM module'. ARITHMETIC CROSS-CHECKS THAT ALL PASS, and they are what make this record trustworthy rather than a single unsourced quote: (a) 38.4 Gbps x 16 bits = 614.4 Gb/s = 76.8 GB/s per direction - the stated rate and the stated width multiply to the stated bandwidth; (b) 1,075.2 / 153.6 = exactly 7 links, matching the '7 AMD Infinity Fabric links' in the ROCm node description (net2-rocm-mi350-microarch), so the aggregate and the per-link figure are mutually consistent; (c) 1,075.2 + 128 = 1,203.2, reproducing AMD's stated total transport rate exactly, where the 128 is the separately-configured PCIe Gen 5 host link. GENERATIONAL MOVEMENT, per direction per link: CDNA 3 / MI300X at 64, CDNA 4 / MI350 at 76.8 - a 1.2x, which AMD itself describes as '20% faster generationally'. Per-direction aggregate across the 7-link fully-connected domain: 448 GB/s on MI300X, 537.6 GB/s on MI350.
topology: Fully connected 8-GPU node, identical to the prior generation. AMD's MI350 microarchitecture reference (net2-rocm-mi350-microarch) states 'a fully connected 8-GPU node topology, identical to the prior generation' with each GPU reaching its 7 peers over 7 Infinity Fabric links at 38.4 Gbps, plus one PCIe Gen 5 x16 link to the host and 'one Infinity Fabric link configured for PCIe Gen 5 to connect to I/O devices such as storage and networking'. MI350X is an air-cooled 1000W OAM on a UBB8 baseboard that is drop-in compatible with the MI325X platform; MI355X is 1400W direct liquid-cooled, and AMD states up to 128 MI355X fit in a 200kW rack. THE PACKAGE-INTERIOR CHANGE IS THE REAL STORY: CDNA 4 consolidates the I/O dies from four in CDNA 3 to two larger ones, and 'the direct connection between the two IODs reduces latency and power consumption compared to the previous generation' - each IOD now carries four links.
switching: No switch part. The scale-up domain is the 8-GPU node, built from direct point-to-point links, exactly as in CDNA 3. Scale-out is handled by external networking. The structural consequence is unchanged from amd-xgmi and amd-infinity-fabric-link: a direct-attached full mesh is non-blocking within its domain size, but there is no fabric to grow past 8, so a wider deployment must add nodes rather than GPUs. AMD's differentiation here is that its 8-way all-to-all domain needs no switch part at all, where NVIDIA reaches the same 8-way shape only by adding NVSwitch silicon (see nvswitch-4).
notes: Added 2026-10-03 because the Infinity Fabric record covered CDNA 3 only, and CDNA 4 is the generation that RESOLVED the direction ambiguity rather than deepening it - the single most useful thing this pass produced for AMD. WHY A SEPARATE RECORD RATHER THAN FOLDING INTO amd-infinity-fabric-link: that record is named '4th generation (MI300/MI325 class)' and its 64 GB/s is the CDNA 3 figure whose direction had to be inferred. Now that AMD states the convention outright, the per-generation values belong on separate records - CDNA 3 at 64 per direction, CDNA 4 at 76.8 - because they differ by 20% and a reader sizing a fabric needs the right one. WHAT AMD PUBLISHES FOR THIS GENERATION (white paper plus ROCm reference): 8 XCDs and 2 IODs on N3P/N6, 'communications with other GPUs through 7 AMD Infinity Fabric links operating at 38.4 Gbps, providing over 1 TB/s of aggregate communication bandwidth per GPU', 288 GB HBM3E at 8 TB/s, 256 MB Infinity Cache, one PCIe Gen 5 x16 host link. INFERENCE RELEVANCE, and it is a positive finding that reverses the usual read of this vendor: AMD's fabric has been closing the gap to NVIDIA's rather than lagging it. 537.6 GB/s per direction across the 7-link domain against NVLink 4's 450 GB/s per direction per GPU means an 8-GPU AMD node now has MORE per-GPU scale-up bandwidth than an 8-GPU Hopper node - 1.2x - while needing no switch silicon and offering a larger 8-GPU all-to-all domain than the 8-GPU direct-attach mesh NVIDIA could build without NVSwitch. The ratio against local memory is what actually decides TP viability, and there AMD is far behind: 537.6 GB/s per direction against MI355X's 8 TB/s of HBM3E is about 15x, versus NVLink 4's 450 against the H100's 3.35 TB/s at about 7.4x. So the honest summary is that AMD has the better fabric-to-GPU-count story and the worse fabric-to-memory-bandwidth story, and since decode is memory-bound at low batch, it is the fabric-to-memory ratio - not the fabric-to-fabric comparison - that sets the TP crossover (see docs/11-interconnect-decision.md). TWO SECONDARY POINTS. First, partitioning interacts with the fabric: AMD's NPS2 mode keeps all memory traffic inside one IOD and its associated XCDs, 'reducing the overhead of crossing the AMD Infinity Fabric network between the two IODs' - so on a 2-way partition you can avoid the fabric entirely for memory traffic, which is a lever that has no analogue on NVIDIA parts and is worth knowing before choosing TP degree on MI355X. Second, MI350P is the PCIe variant with 4 XCDs, one IOD, 144 GB and up to 8 cards per air-cooled server, and the ROCm page gives it no Infinity Fabric GPU-to-GPU path - so MI350P has NO scale-up fabric in the sources retrieved and should not be treated as an 8-GPU scale-up part.
